knowledge:
- key_parameters: transform=Logical indicating whether to apply a hyperbolic arcsine transformation to all non-clusterID channels ;; cofactor=Numeric value specifying the cofactor to use in the arcsinh transformation (e.g., 15 for mass cytometry) ;; choose.markers=Logical indicating whether to prompt the user in the console to select specific markers ;; markers=Character specifying markers to include (e.g., "all" or "1:25") ;; choose.ref=Logical indicating whether to prompt the user to choose alternative reference populations ;; zero.ref=Logical indicating whether to use a zero/synthetic negative reference to show positive enrichments ;; rename.markers=Logical indicating whether to prompt the user to rename markers ;; new.marker.names=Character specifying new names for markers (e.g., "none" or a comma-separated string) ;; IQR.thresh=Numeric threshold to avoid artificial inflation of MEM values due to small IQR (defaults to 0.5) ;; file.is.clust=Logical indicating whether each input file contains cells from only one cluster ;; add.fileID=Logical indicating whether to append a file ID to each cell's cluster ID when file.is.clust is FALSE ;; cluster.MEM=Character specifying clustering option for the MEM heatmap (e.g., "both") ;; cluster.medians=Character specifying clustering option for the medians heatmap (e.g., "none") ;; display.thresh=Numeric (0-10) specifying the threshold for displaying markers in the MEM label ;; output.files=Logical indicating whether to write output files (PDFs, txt matrices) to an "output files" folder
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing single-cell datasets (e.g., flow cytometry, mass cytometry) where cell populations or clusters have already been identified, and you want to automatically generate quantitative, standardized, and easily interpretable labels describing marker enrichment for each population.
- pitfalls: If a population has a very small IQR due to background level expression, it can artificially inflate the MEM value; a default IQR threshold of 0.5 is set to prevent this, and changing it is not recommended unless the user deeply understands the dataset. If using multiple files with file.is.clust=FALSE, ensure the last column of each file specifies the cluster IDs. Row names (MEM labels) on the generated MEM heatmap may be cut off due to window dimensions; users should save the image as a PDF or check the "enrichment score-rownames.txt" file to view full labels. Applying different cofactors to different channels (common in fluorescence flow cytometry) should be done prior to MEM analysis with transform=FALSE.

workflows.name: marker_enrichment_modeling_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform Marker Enrichment Modeling (MEM) analysis on single-cell data to generate quantitative population labels, visualize them via heatmaps, and calculate similarity scores between populations.
input: cell_data.csv (a single-cell expression matrix where rows are cells, columns are markers, and the last column is the cluster ID)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the single-cell dataset ;; 2. Run MEM analysis using the MEM function ;; 3. Generate population labels and heatmaps using the build_heatmaps function ;; 4. Calculate similarity (RMSD) scores between populations using the MEM_RMSD function
workflows.code:
library(cytoMEM)
data(PBMC)
head(PBMC)

MEM_values <-
  MEM(
    PBMC,
    transform = TRUE,
    cofactor = 15,
    # Change choose.markers to TRUE to see and select channels in console
    choose.markers = FALSE,
    markers = "all",
    choose.ref = FALSE,
    zero.ref = FALSE,
    # Change rename.markers to TRUE to see and choose new names for channels in console
    rename.markers = FALSE,
    new.marker.names = "none",
    IQR.thresh = NULL
  )

build_heatmaps(
  MEM_values,
  cluster.MEM = "both",
  cluster.medians = "none",
  cluster.IQRs = "none",
  display.thresh = 1,
  output.files = FALSE,
  labels = FALSE,
  only.MEMheatmap = FALSE)

MEM_RMSD(
  MEM_values[[5]][[1]],
  format=NULL,
  output.matrix=FALSE)
